standard_text: Modes of excretion – ammonotelism, ureotelism, uricotelism; human excretory system – structure and function; urine formation, osmoregulation; regulation of kidney function – renin–angiotensin, atrial natriuretic factor, ADH and diabetes insipidus; role of other organs in excretion; disorders – uraemia, renal failure, renal calculi, nephritis; dialysis and artificial kidney, kidney transplant.

key_big: Filtration → reabsorption → secretion in the nephron.
key_sub: ADH, aldosterone and ANF regulate the kidney.
body_html:
How to think about it

Animals excrete ammonia (aquatic animals), urea (mammals, adult frogs) or uric acid (birds, reptiles, insects). The human kidney has about a million nephrons. Blood is filtered in the glomerulus (about 180 L of filtrate a day, GFR 125 mL/min), and the tubules reabsorb most of it, leaving about 1.5 L of urine.

The counter-current mechanism of the loop of Henle and vasa recta keeps the medulla salty so concentrated urine can form. ADH increases water reabsorption; the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system raises blood pressure; ANF lowers it.

Example

Birds excrete mainly?

least water

Answer: uric acid

Example

Hormone that saves water?

vasopressin

Answer: ADH

Common mistakes

  • Saying urea is made in the kidney.
  • Saying the ascending limb lets water out.
  • Calling humans uricotelic.

faq.q: Why do birds excrete uric acid?
faq.a: It is insoluble and not very toxic, so it can be removed with very little water.
It makes the DCT and collecting duct more permeable to water, so more water is reabsorbed and urine is concentrated.
